messages:
maya: quick heads-up — onboarding taurus-9b (ported from hpq weights) shows a rerank/qa quality drop after int8 quant + our rotary->ALiBi adapter. quick numbers from local eval: gemma-7b baseline MRR@10=0.48, taurus fp16 MRR@10=0.47, taurus int8 w/ adapter MRR@10=0.39 :confused:
andre: ouch. do you have a short sample prompt + outputs? could be tokenization or pos encoding mismatch.
maya: sample prompt below and two completions (fp16 vs int8)
maya: prompt: "Summarize the legal risks of an open-source dataset scraped from forums."
maya: fp16: "Main risks include PII leakage, copyright, and inaccurate technical claims leading to liability. Mitigation: redaction, rights checks, provenance headers." 
maya: int8+adapter: "Risks involve dataset quality and policy compliance. Solutions: monitoring and filtering." <-- noticeably shorter, misses legal specifics
sophia: that smells like the adapter compresses long-range amplitude on rotary -> ALiBi conversion. Did you check logits distribution / logits temperature after quant?
maya: i dumped logits for top tokens for the phrase "PII leakage". fp16 top token probs ~ [0.24,0.12,0.05], int8 top probs ~ [0.09,0.08,0.07] — distribution is flatter.
buildbot: [ci-eval] taurus/int8-adapter smoke: 100 prompts ran, avg MRR@10 0.395 (-0.08 vs fp16). see /artifacts/1754321999/summary.txt
andre: @raj can you look at the kv-cache handling? if rotary->ALiBi mapping rewrites slopes per head maybe headwise scaling got quantized badly.
raj: looking. first thought — our adapter assumes rotary freq == model.head_dim/2 mapping. some taurus variants use a nonstandard freq schedule (sparser). i'll inspect the state-dict header.
raj: quick inspect: state keys include "rotary.freqs" with shape (128,) and values are non-monotonic. adapter code currently does linear resample. that could create aliasing after int8.
sophia: try preserving freqs and compute ALiBi slopes from actual freqs instead of resampling. small patch suggestion:

sophia: ```python
# pos_adapter.py (snippet)
def freqs_to_alibi_slopes(freqs, heads):
    # preserve shape, derive slope per head from median freq chunk
    chunk = len(freqs)//heads
    slopes = [float(freqs[i*chunk:(i+1)*chunk].mean()) for i in range(heads)]
    return np.array(slopes, dtype=np.float32)
```

sophia: then run quant calibration with the new slopes.
maya: updated adapter locally and reran a 50-prompt smoke. results: MRR@10 int8 -> 0.435 (was 0.395), length and specifics improved, still 0.035 gap vs fp16.
andre: nice improvement. remaining gap might be quant clipping on per-head scale. try per-head symmetric quant (scale per head) instead of global per-tensor.
raj: agreed. i'll push a tiny per-head quant experiment into bench harness. running now.
buildbot: [ci-eval] per-head-int8 experiment queued (job 1754322005). ETA ~15m :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maya: thanks all. next steps: commit adapter change, run full eval, follow-up if per-head quant doesn't close gap. filing a tiny RFC for the adapter logic so Dedicated/Private runtimes get same treatment. :thumbsup:
